reasons: F23, F21: recently public via SPAC with capital raising in the year; de-SPAC companies often have immature controls and strong pressure to meet projections, and F03 shows no auditor ICFR attestation to test this.

F08, F09, F10: revenue is recognised over time, contract assets/unbilled amounts are significant, and channel return rights or bill-and-hold arrangements exist; together these leave a lot of room for judgement in revenue timing (e.g. hardware vs software bundles).
F11: material related-party transactions add a further risk of revenue or cost misstatement.
F07: an immaterial revision of prior periods shows errors were already found, which is often an early sign of weak close processes.
R04, R02: sales grew 63% (SGI 1.63) while gross margin improved (GMI 0.72); fast growth with improving margins at a young company deserves scrutiny of revenue cut-off and cost allocation.
R07, R13: leverage rose sharply (LVGI 1.71) and soft assets are high (0.72), which leaves more room for discretionary estimates.

R01, R18, R11: receivables fell relative to sales (DSRI 0.52; AR growth minus sales growth -0.78), which argues against aggressive recognition through receivables; but with significant contract assets (F09), the risk may sit in unbilled balances instead.

R09, R17, R08, R10, R19: the Beneish M-score (-3.18) is well below its threshold, the F-score is low (0.41), and accruals are negative while cash flow is large relative to income; these quantitative models give mostly reassuring signals and keep the score from going higher.
F01, F04, F05, F14, F16, F17, F24: no reported material weakness, going concern, auditor change, executive turnover, investigations or critical audit matters (CAMs).
